DECLINED nonetheless, and on owner law rather than against the bytes: a unit running Lam.2.13-Lam.2.19 necessarily puts a row seam at Lam.2.12/Lam.2.13, and that seam ANSWERS a question the owner holds open, whether the narrator's first person gives way to the address at Lam.2.13 or already at Lam.2.11. A ruling may adopt a span that RESPECTS a held-open region; it may not decide one. The proposed unit would also submerge the second held question inside itself - the addressee of the imperatives that open with צָעַ֥ק לִבָּ֖ם (oshb:Lam.2.18, byte tier) and run second-person feminine singular through Lam.2.19 - by removing the seam at which it is currently held. Two further tier-1 signals cut inside the proposed unit and would go unargued: the first-person drop at Lam.2.14 and the turn to second-person feminine singular imperatives at Lam.2.18. The addressee chain is a real tier-1 continuity; it is disclosed at both seams, not made into a span.

docket.grounds: Upheld on bytes, five ways. (i) The three-token form בְּי֥וֹם אַף יְהוָ֖ה (oshb:Lam.2.22, byte tier) stands in exactly 1 verse book-wide (sweep: 1 verse, byte tier, verses containing the three-token form) - the digit and its object are both right, and a form attested once cannot function as a refrain; the prose label and the refrain-shaped signal key both encode that error, and refrain-grade evidence is tier-1, so the mislabel is load-bearing. (ii) The claim that the opening petition repeats an earlier one carries no ref, no tier and no digit, although the byte ground is exact and available: רְאֵ֤ה יְהוָה֙ וְֽהַבִּ֔יטָה (oshb:Lam.2.20, byte tier) stands verbatim in exactly 2 verses book-wide (sweep: 2 verses, byte tier: Lam.1.11 and Lam.2.20). (iii) A parashah mark is named inside an observed-signal key, where the single-witness tier-3 disclosure belongs in prose only. (iv) The high confidence rests on assigning Lam.2.20-Lam.2.22 to the personified city, but its 1cs speaker and 2ms addressee are equally available to the poem's own narrator, whose 1cs already stands at עֵינַי֙ (oshb:Lam.2.11, byte tier) with 1cs verbs addressing the city at oshb:Lam.2.13; the forms do not separate the two (tier-1 speaker and addressee marking). (v) Both-sides law at the front seam: the imperative to pour out the heart before the Lord at Lam.2.19 and the prayer that answers it at Lam.2.20 bind across the cut, and the same divine title stands at Lam.2.19 and inside Lam.2.20 - undisclosed. REFINED: the challenge's supporting ground, that the close and the alef line share no attested spelling, is byte-false. The token בְּי֥וֹם is byte-identical at Lam.2.1 and Lam.2.22 (sweep: 2 verses, byte tier), each followed by an anger word - בְּי֥וֹם אַפּֽוֹ (oshb:Lam.2.1, byte tier) closing the alef line against בְּי֥וֹם אַף יְהוָ֖ה (oshb:Lam.2.22, byte tier) closing the tav line. The wrath inclusio the reading asserts is real and citable at byte tier; the defect is that it is asserted at no level, not that it is wrong. Severity stays medium.
